summary: José Carlos Ribeiro Calazans Duarte is an indologist and historian-archaeologist. He completed his doctorate at Lusófona University, among degrees from institutions such as Lisbon and EPHE, and served as an Assistant Professor at Lusófona University from 2006 to 2021.

José Ignacio Cabezón, a scholar of Buddhist, Tibetan, and religious studies, earned his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa. He taught at Iliff School of Theology before becoming the Dalai Lama Professor at UC Santa Barbara in 2001.

José Ventura Traveset (1862–1941) was a Spanish scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Francisco García Ayuso. He served as Professor of Humanities at the University of Granada (1887–1889) and became a Professor at the University of Valencia in 1901.
Jotika Khur-Yearn is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Kate Crosby.

Jowita Kramer is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who earned her doctorate under Lambert Schmithausen at the University of Hamburg. She has held posts at the University of Munich (2017–2021) and the University of Leipzig as Professor (2021).

Joy Brennan is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology who earned a PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under teachers including Paul Mendes-Flohr, Richard Rosengarten, and Constance Furey.

Joyce Burkhalter Flueckiger is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied at Goshen College and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, later serving as Professor Emerita at Emory University from around 1992.

Joydeb Dinda is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy who earned a Ph.D. at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda Educational and Research Institute by 2022 and became an Assistant Professor at Laxmi Devi Shroff Adarsh Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya that year.

Jozef Deleu (1925–1994) was an indologist who earned his doctorate under Adriaan Scharpé at Ghent University and also studied at Hamburg. He served as docent in Indology at Ghent University from 1964 to 1990.

João Carlos Barbosa Gonçalves is an indologist, linguist, and philosopher who earned his PhD in Linguistics from the University of São Paulo. He held professorships at the State University of Campinas (2003–2005) and the University of São Paulo (2014–2015).

Juan Gelabert y Gordiola (1843–1894) was an indologist and linguist who studied under Francisco García Ayuso and earned his Ph.D. at Complutense University of Madrid, where he later served as Professor of Sanskrit from 1883 to 1894.
Juan Wu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Cardiff University under the doctoral supervision of Max Deeg.

Judit Törzsök is an indologist who earned her DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. She served as Associate Professor at University of Lille III and became directrice d’études at École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2018.

Judith Simmer-Brown is a scholar of Buddhist, Tibetan, and religious studies who earned a PhD from Walden University and studied under Chögyam Trungpa. Since 1977, she has served at Naropa University, where she is Distinguished Professor Emerita.

Judith Snodgrass is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her BA and PhD at the University of Sydney and served as an Associate Professor at Western Sydney University from 1991 to 2016.

Juhn Y. Ahn is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley in 2007. Ahn serves as Associate Professor of Buddhist and Korean Studies at the University of Michigan.

Juhyung Rhi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of California, Berkeley. In 1992, Rhi was appointed Professor of Art History at Seoul National University.
Juichiro Tanabe is a scholar of philosophy who was a PhD candidate at the University of Bradford between 2000 and 2001 and studied under traditional teacher Richard Hunn.

Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire (1805–1895) was a French scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held the chair of Greek and Latin philosophy at the Collège de France from 1838 to 1852.

Jules Bloch (1880–1953) was a French indologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Antoine Meillet. He was a professor at INALCO, directeur d’études at EPHE, and Chair of Sanskrit at the Collège de France (1936–1951).
